As of my last update in October 2023, the 2024 United States Senate election in Utah is set to take place on November 5, 2024. This election will determine who will occupy the U.S. Senate seat from Utah currently held by Mitt Romney, a Republican who was elected in 2018.

Mitt Romney announced in September 2023 that he would not seek re-election, which opens the field for new candidates from both major parties and possibly third-party or independent candidates. Romney's decision not to run for another term could lead to a competitive primary, given Utah's strong Republican leaning.

Potential Republican candidates might include prominent state politicians or business figures, considering the state's Republican tilt. Utah has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since Frank Moss in 1970, so the Republican primary is often seen as the more decisive contest.

On the Democratic side, potential candidates had not formally announced their intentions by the time of the latest information, but historically, Democrats in Utah face an uphill battle due to the state's conservative lean. 

There may also be candidates from other political affiliations, including independents and third-party challengers, though these are typically less prominent in Utah's political landscape.

For the most up-to-date information on candidates and developments in this election, you should check recent news sources and official announcements from the candidates or relevant political parties.
